title: Each individual in the list is given an identifying number. The numbers following an individual’s name are the identifying numbers for the parents. Three dot 5s rather than a number are used for a missing parent.

illustrates.quote: Ascending Ancestral and Pedigree Charts a. Transcribe ancestral and pedigree charts as lists, using 1-3 margins. Begin with the most current item or person and move backward through the generations. Assign a number to each name or item in the chart, beginning with the most current. List them sequentially, moving back through each generation, in the same direction as the chart. Sequential numeric identification allows the ascending parentage to be followed without using a tactile graphic. b. Follow each item with any information specific to the item or individual, e.g., dates of birth/death, etc. Immediately follow this information with the two numbers from the list that represents the parent(s). Use a comma to separate the two numbers. Use three dot 5s to represent the missing connection if only one parent is listed. c. Insert a transcriber’s note about the parentage numbers. Sample:
